Apex Industrial Machinery Corp. - Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Industrial Machinery Corp. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. To ask a question, you will need to press star one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star two. Please limit yourself to one question and one follow-up. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Jenkins, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Jenkins (Head of Investor Relations):
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Apex Industrial Machinery Corp.'s results for the third quarter of 2024. Joining me on today's call are Johnathan Hale, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Rivera, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Operating Officer; and Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking in nature and subject to certain risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Johnathan Hale.

Johnathan Hale (CEO):
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report on Apex Industrial Machinery Corp.'s performance for the third quarter. As a leader in precision manufacturing equipment—including CNC machining centers, industrial automation systems, and heavy-duty material handling solutions—we've made significant progress on several fronts. We've delivered robust organic revenue growth alongside strategic inorganic contributions from acquisitions, hit strong total revenue figures with double-digit year-over-year increases, advanced our share repurchase program with disciplined execution, shortened lead times across key products and components, built a record backlog with solid conversion rates and positive order intake expectations, and accelerated growth in our automation and digital offerings, which are driving meaningful efficiency gains.

These achievements reflect broad-based strength across our segments, fueled by secular tailwinds like Industry 4.0 transformations, U.S. manufacturing reshoring, and rising demand for electrification and automation. We're confident that our strategic initiatives are positioning us for long-term sustainable growth.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Michael Rivera to provide more detail on our financial results.

Michael Rivera (CFO):
Thank you, Johnathan. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining our Q3 2024 earnings call. I'll dive right into our top-line performance, which continues to reflect the strength of our positioning in the industrial equipment market amid a robust capex recovery cycle. For the third quarter, total revenue reached $2.1 billion, representing a 13% year-over-year increase. On an organic basis—excluding a modest foreign exchange tailwind—we delivered 11% growth, underscoring the underlying health of our core operations. This marks our sixth consecutive quarter of double-digit growth.

Let me break this down starting with organic revenue growth, which came in at a strong 8% year-over-year. This excludes the impact of recent acquisitions, FX fluctuations—which provided a 1% tailwind—and one-time items. Organically, we saw broad-based strength across our core segments. In Machine Tools and Precision Equipment, which is 52% of revenue, we grew 9%, propelled by higher volumes of our next-gen HyperMill 5000 series 5-axis CNC machines, with shipments up 12% year-over-year, particularly from automotive OEMs upgrading for EV components. Backlog here is at a record $1.2 billion, up 15% sequentially.

Automation and Robotics, 28% of revenue, delivered a standout 14% organic growth, driven by our collaborative robot arms integrated with proprietary EdgeAI software for predictive maintenance, seeing 20% volume uptake from e-commerce fulfillment centers and food & beverage processors. Material Handling and Heavy Equipment, 20% of revenue, achieved 5% organic growth, offset by strength in our redesigned ElectroLift palletizers with 30% higher energy efficiency.

Regionally, North America at 45% of revenue grew 10% organically, benefiting from infrastructure spending and data center bookings up 25%. EMEA at 30% grew 7%, driven by green energy transitions like wind turbine gear hobbing machines for Vestas and aerospace recovery. Asia-Pacific at 25% saw 6% growth, with India and Southeast Asia surging 12% on semiconductor expansions despite softer China demand.

Key initiatives include our $150 million year-to-date R&D in digital twins and IoT-enabled smart factories. Our FactoryOS platform, deployed in over 500 sites, has a 15% attach rate for software subscriptions, lifting recurring revenue to 18% of organic sales with 75% gross margins.

Shifting to inorganic contributions from acquisitions, these added 4 percentage points to total growth, or about $85 million in Q3. Our $320 million acquisition of RoboForge Systems delivered $65 million, with 120% year-over-year growth and $12 million in annualized synergies. The $180 million EuroTech Drives purchase added $30 million, growing 15% organically post-close, enhancing our electrification portfolio.

These were financed with 60% cash and 40% from our revolver, keeping net leverage at 1.8x EBITDA. Looking forward, we expect Q4 organic growth of 7-9%, with a $4.1 billion backlog up 18% year-over-year.

Our Machinery segment generated strong results, up 18% year-over-year, with a book-to-bill of 1.28x and backlog at $3.2 billion. Aftermarket parts and services, 42% of mix, grew 9%, supported by our 150,000-machine installed base at 82% utilization and IoT-enabled ApexConnect driving 25% subscription growth.

Gross margin was 32%, driven by pricing discipline, mix shift to digital, and supply chain efficiencies. Operating expenses were $450 million, resulting in operating income of $320 million. Net income was $210 million, or $1.85 per share.

We're managing capital allocation effectively. On our share repurchase program, authorized at $1.0 billion in February, we've executed $425 million to date, or 42.5%, retiring 14.5 million shares at an average $44.75. Year-to-date, $650 million across programs. Quarterly: Q1 $150 million at $42.10, Q2 $175 million at $45.20, Q3 $225 million at $46.50, or 22% of quarterly FCF. We use Rule 10b5-1 plans for VWAP executions at 1.2% of daily volume, buying below 10x forward EV/EBITDA.

This aligns with regional dynamics, aggressive in North America on infrastructure, measured in Europe amid energy issues, lighter in Asia for M&A. Repurchases are 35% of FCF, balancing dividends up 8% to $0.42/share, debt reduction, and growth capex. EPS accretion was $0.12 in Q3, $0.45 full-year. Remaining authorization $575 million, expecting $200-250 million in Q4.

We prioritize investments in high-growth areas and returning capital to shareholders. Next, I'll hand over to Lisa Chen, our COO, for an operational update.

Lisa Chen (COO):
Thank you, Michael. Operationally, we've focused on improving productivity and efficiency across our manufacturing facilities. We've implemented lean principles and data analytics for process optimization, while investing in technologies for supply chain resilience.

Today, I'd like to address lead times for key products and components, a critical metric amid supply chain volatility. Our weighted average lead time across core lines has improved to 14.2 weeks, down 18% sequentially from 17.3 weeks and 32% from the 21-week peak last year. This positions us well versus peers.

For modular CNC machining centers, 28% of bookings, lead times are 10 weeks, thanks to our Chillicothe facility ramp. Hydraulic excavators and telehandlers, 35% of mix, are at 16 weeks, aided by steel stabilization and inventory builds. Electronic control modules and PLCs fell to 9.5 weeks, with dual-sourcing reducing Asian reliance by 40%. Precision castings are at 11 weeks, with AI-optimized scrap rates under 2%.

This is our third straight quarter of double-digit gains, with 88% capacity utilization, 62 days finished goods inventory, and 8.1x turns. Our $250 million Supply Chain Resilience Program is paying off.

Regionally, North America averages 13 weeks on nearshoring; Europe 16.5 weeks despite Red Sea issues; Asia-Pacific 18 weeks but gaining share. Technically, our Digital Twin Initiative with Siemens NX cuts forecasting errors by 35%, AI/ML demand sensing hits 92% accuracy, and vendor scorecards ensure OTIF. We've verticalized 20% of castings in Mexico.

Shorter leads boost our 1.25x book-to-bill, targeting $1.2 billion Q4 revenue recognition, lifting margins to 32.5%. We guide Q4 to 13-14 weeks, with sub-12 potential in H1 2025.

On order intake and backlog conversion, Q3 intake hit $1.25 billion, up 18% year-over-year and 5% sequentially, with book-to-bill at 1.22x. Backlog is $4.7 billion, up 22%, over 10 months visibility. 55% in high-margin automation, 28% services-attached.

We converted 68% of beginning backlog to revenue in 12 months, 92% in 24 months. Q4 intake expected at $1.3-1.4 billion, FY24 16-18% growth, FY25 10-13% organic.

Americas 52% of intake, 20%+ growth on IRA electrification; EMEA mid-single digits; APAC 25%+ on semis. Factory 4.0 platform cuts lead times 25%, CTO modules lift new order conversion to 75%.

We're prioritizing quality backlog for 12-15% CAGR through FY27.

And I would like to turn the call over to our CTO, Dr. Elena Vasquez, for an update on our technology roadmap.

Dr. Elena Vasquez (CTO):
Thank you, Lisa. We are committed to driving innovation and developing cutting-edge solutions for our customers. We are investing in R&D in artificial intelligence, machine learning, and the Internet of Things.

Our Automation and Digital Offerings segment grew 28% year-over-year to $1.2 billion, 22% of revenue, with recurring at 65% growing 42%. FactoryOS saw 35% adoption.

Efficiency gains include 92% failure prediction accuracy, cutting downtime 32%; digital twins boosting throughput 18-22%; AutoGreen slashing energy 25%. Gross margins at 38%, up 450 bps.

North America up 32% on labor shortages and CHIPS; Asia-Pacific 25% on PLI; Europe 22% on Industrie 4.0. R&D at $250 million funds 5G MES and gen AI. Partnerships with NVIDIA and AWS.

We guide 25-30% growth FY24, $1.1 billion recurring, 200 bps margin expansion.

Our new FactoryOS platform is showing promising early results, with significant impact on customer OEE and our market positioning. We believe these technologies will transform the industrial landscape and create significant opportunities for Apex.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. Our first question comes from David Lee with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

David Lee (Morgan Stanley):
Good morning. Can you elaborate on the growth drivers in your digital solutions business?

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Absolutely, David. Our digital solutions, like FactoryOS and IndusPredict, are central to the 28% segment growth. Predictive maintenance with 92% accuracy has reduced customer downtime by 32%, while digital twins optimize throughput by 18-22%. Adoption is up 35% in our installed base, with recurring revenue at 65% of the segment. This is outpacing the IIoT market, driven by AI/ML on 15 petabytes of data and partnerships like NVIDIA for edge AI. Regionally, North America leads with reshoring, but Asia and Europe follow strongly on policy tailwinds.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Carter with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter (Goldman Sachs):
What are your plans for expanding your presence in emerging markets?

Johnathan Hale:
Thanks, Emily. Emerging markets, especially India and Southeast Asia, contributed to our 12% APAC surge outside China. We're leveraging PLI schemes for solar and electronics, with new assembly in Indonesia capturing share in palm oil and semis. Backlog conversion is strong at 72% in Americas but accelerating in APAC. M&A pipeline includes tuck-ins there, balancing with nearshoring in Mexico. Overall, targeting 10-13% organic in FY25, with dual-sourcing mitigating risks.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Robert Kim with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Robert Kim (JPMorgan):
How are you addressing the skilled labor shortage in the manufacturing sector?

Lisa Chen:
Great question, Robert. Labor shortages are pushing automation uptake, up 32% in North America. Our cobots and EdgeAI reduce reliance on skilled workers, while digital twins and AI demand sensing optimize staffing. Workforce programs include training on Industry 4.0 tools, with utilization at 88%. Vendor partnerships and vertical integration, like Monterrey castings, free up resources. This supports 82% machine utilization and NPS of 68.

Operator:
Thank you. There are no further questions at this time.

Johnathan Hale:
Thank you for your questions and your interest in Apex Industrial Machinery Corp. We are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain focused on executing our strategy and delivering long-term value for our shareholders.

Sarah Jenkins:
Thank you, everyone, for joining us today. This concludes our earnings call. Have a great day.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for participating. You may now disconnect.
